lead: The tab bar of open pages common in admin apps: switch, close, pin, drag to reorder, a context menu (close others / to the left / to the right / all, pin, refresh) and scroll buttons at both ends when there are too many. It knows nothing about routing: the tabs are data (`tabs` + `activeKey`), and clicks and closes come back through callbacks. Together with `KeepAlive`, pages you switch away from keep their state.

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: Click a tab to switch; close it with × or the middle button, right-click for more, drag to reorder. Keyboard: arrow keys move the focus, Delete closes, Alt + left / right reorders. The first tab (home) is pinned and can't be closed.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: `card` (small bordered cards), `chrome` (browser tabs, the selected one joins the content below) and `line` (an underline).

keep-alive.title: With KeepAlive
keep-alive.description: Each page holds a counter, an input and some tall content: they all survive switching tabs, scroll position included. The state goes only when the tab is closed; right-click → Refresh starts the page over.
keep-alive.placeholder: Type here, switch away and back
keep-alive.note: Closing a tab drops its page state; right-click → Refresh remounts it.

overflow.title: Overflow
overflow.description: When the tabs don't fit, scroll buttons appear at both ends; the active tab scrolls into view.

tab.key: Unique identifier, usually the page's path
tab.title: The tab's title (also its accessible name and tooltip)
tab.pinned: Pinned: placed first, can't be closed, and only reorders among pinned tabs (e.g. home)

helpers.title: Helpers
helpers.closeTabs: Closes a set of tabs; closing the active one switches to the next tab in its place (or the previous one). Pinned / non-closable tabs stay
helpers.keysToClose: Works out which tabs to close for a scope (`self` / `others` / `left` / `right` / `all`)
helpers.moveTab: Moves a tab; pinned and normal tabs each stay in their own zone
helpers.openTab: Opens a tab: returns the list unchanged if it's already open, else appends it

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.item: A tab + its close button: `data-active`, `data-pinned`, `data-dragging`; while dragging, the offset is `--drag-x`
styling.title: Icon and title
styling.close: The close button, outside the tab (a button can't contain another one)
styling.scroll: The scroll buttons at both ends when there are too many tabs, `data-direction=start|end`
styling.keepAlive: One pane per item (scrolling on its own), the current one has `data-active`; the root has `data-transition`
